title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting and notation. Ab_* denotes simplicial abelian groups and Ab_· denotes (non-negatively graded) chain complexes. C_*(X) = Z[X] is the free simplicial abelian group on a simplicial set X, and C_·(X) is its normalized chain complex. DP is the Dold–Puppe (Dold–Kan) equivalence between Ab_· and Ab_*; 'ND' is presumably its inverse, normalization N. This page closes items (c)–(d) of a numbered discussion and opens item (e). The page is numbered 17 in Grothendieck's own pagination; the archive number 319 is written at bottom left.

(c)–(d) The universal description. A contravariant functor F: Δ̂^op → Ab that turns colimits of simplicial sets into limits is determined by its values on the standard simplices. It is therefore given by an object K_* of Ab_*, with F(X) ≅ Hom_{Ab_*}(C_*(X), K_*).
- Grothendieck phrases this as follows. There is a universal functor F_0: Δ̂^op → (Ab_*)^op, defined by F_0^op(X) = C_*(X). Every such F is obtained by applying to F_0 an operation Ω^* (with an inserted annotation of the form 'Ω^* ∈ U^L'; reading uncertain).
- Dually, covariant functors Δ̂ → Ab of the same kind are obtained from the universal covariant functor X ↦ C_*(X) in Ab_* by applying an operation Ω_*: Ab_* → Ab.
- There are equivalent formulations with Ω^·, Ω_· acting on chain complexes. These are obtained by replacing C_*(X) by the normalized chains C_·(X), via DP.
- The previous page notes that this also works for an arbitrary index category in place of Δ, and in a non-additive context.
- The surrounding framework is the 'U_L' / 'C^{[n]}' machinery: functors encoded by families of objects with operations.

(e) What role does DP play? This is a methodological comparison.
- Chain complexes are easier to describe ('one easily gets lost in describing semi-simplicial objects!').
- The chain-complex index category L_· is much 'smaller' than L_*, which appears as a 'plethoric version' of L.
- A left-margin note qualifies this, apparently: subject to checking that it can be expressed in terms of kernels of projectors. This alludes to the normalized complex as the image of an idempotent, i.e. to Dold–Kan through idempotent splitting.
- Nevertheless, the multiplicative structures differ. The degreewise tensor product on Ab_* and the tensor product of complexes on Ab_· do not correspond under DP/N. The simplicial one is the simpler to handle and imposes itself in what follows; the one on Ab_· hardly enters.
- The non-additive functors Λ^i, Γ^i, Sym^i extend degreewise and trivially to Ab_*. On Ab_· they are essentially unavailable except by transport of structure through DP. The divided powers Γ^i are exactly what the PD de Rham complex project needs.
- Conclusion: the simplicial side will be the essential working framework.
errors: No real error. The statement that the multiplicative structures 'do not correspond' under DP/N is true strictly. They do correspond up to coherent homotopy (Eilenberg–Zilber, Alexander–Whitney/shuffle maps; N is lax monoidal), which the page does not mention.
The 'smallness' advantage of Ab_· is heuristic; the margin itself flags it as conditional ('sous réserve...').

ideas.what: Colimit-to-limit (contravariant) functors on simplicial sets are represented by simplicial abelian groups via the universal functor X ↦ Z[X]
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda/Kan extension; representability of cochain-type functors (e.g. cochains with coefficients in a simplicial abelian group)

ideas.what: Equivalence of the formulations via the Dold–Kan/Dold–Puppe correspondence, Ab_* ≃ Ab_·
Degreewise tensor product on simplicial abelian groups vs tensor product of complexes are not matched by DP/N
ideas.modern_name: Eilenberg–Zilber; monoidal Dold–Kan only up to homotopy (Schwede–Shipley)

ideas.what: Non-additive functors Λ^i, Γ^i, Sym^i are defined directly (degreewise) on simplicial objects but only via DP on complexes
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Puppe derived functors of non-additive functors; simplicial methods for divided powers (Illusie)

ideas.what: Margin: describing chain complexes via kernels of projectors
ideas.modern_name: Normalized complex as image of an idempotent; Dold–Kan in idempotent-complete additive categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold; Lurie (Higher Algebra, Dold–Kan for idempotent-complete categories)

deep.surprise_reason: This is methodological commentary on the Dold–Kan correspondence and on why simplicial abelian groups are preferable to chain complexes for tensor and divided-power operations. That is standard knowledge since Dold–Puppe and Illusie. The universal-functor reformulation is routine Kan extension.
transcription_corrections: 'l'avantage de A_· sur A_*' should read 'Ab_· sur Ab_*'.
'-ssentiellement impérieuse' is the continuation of a hyphenated 'de façon e-ssentiellement', i.e. 'de façon essentiellement impérieuse'.
'par DP et ND' likely denotes DP and its inverse normalization N.
The insertion near Ω^* reads roughly 'via Ω^* ∈ U^L' (refers to the U_L classes of the previous page) rather than '⊗'.
'(dans le cas de Ab_* disons)' appears as 'Ab_{*x}/Ab_{x}' in the image; it compares Ab_* and Ab_·.
'Du fait en travaillant' is uncertain; possibly 'D'abord, en travaillant'.
The left margin likely reads 'Sous réserve de voir ... pour ... en termes des Ker de projecteurs !'.
The number 319 at bottom left is an archive pagination.
